Two independent Claude Cowork sessions converged on the identical finding and fix in real time; the collision was caught by this trail's own Checker (correctly FAILing rather than fabricating authorship) before anything was lost, and resolved by asking the human rather than guessing.
earned_constraints: when two governed sessions can be active on the same repo at once, a Checker must verify a change's actual provenance (git diff timing, unexplained new files) before crediting it to its own trail - detecting an outside actor's uncommitted edit and refusing to claim it is exactly what caught this collision before either session overwrote the other

BLOCKED is the correct disposition for a cross-session authorship question - it is not this trail's authority to decide whether a concurrent process is benign; only the human could answer that, and the trail correctly stopped and surfaced it instead of guessing SEAL or RETRY
